findings.message: Identity and wardrobe override are now persisted via hero_identity and use_signature_outfit properties. CharacterCustomization.from_dict() correctly reads these values from saved state.
findings.resolution: CharacterCustomization persists hero_identity and use_signature_outfit; legacy saves retain swatches.

findings.message: Face swaps and identity changes properly cache the visual tier, clear stale bone-anchor references, and rebuild tool visuals on the replacement skeleton. _apply_hero_identity_layer() creates new identity layer with backpack and clothing materials.
findings.resolution: Visual tier cached, anchor cleared during rig replacement, tool rebuilt on new skeleton.

findings.message: UV/colour heuristics and the generic Kenney source rig cannot achieve the Ziemek patterned-hoodie, detailed-backpack, child-proportioned concept direction. Current code recolours base albedo but lacks patterned textures and child proportions.
findings.resolution: Requires rig-compatible authored garment/child-hero assets for both Ziemek (turquoise graphic hoodie, dark trousers, backpack) and Gniewko (light top/dark-trouser silhouette) plus close and third-person captures.
findings.next_step: Create or obtain authored GLB models matching concept art; integrate into player_controller identity system; capture third-person and close-up evidence.

findings.message: Initial test coverage added for held-tool-after-face-swap and P2/Gniewko grounded split-screen contracts. However, rendered close-up and speech evidence remain open.
findings.resolution: Add held-tool-after-face-swap and P2/Gniewko contracts. Still need rendered close-up (facial) and speech playback evidence.

findings.message: BASE_FOV (55.0) and SPRINT_FOV (59.0) constants align with composed third-person opening camera. Ziemek hoodie color (#30373a), pants, and backpack badge lime accent are defined as constants.

FacialPerformance uses BoneAttachment3D for humanoid rigs to prevent detached face during animations. Static attach_kenney_humanoid() and attach_to_bone() methods handle both rigged and primitive models.

summary: VS-046 code implementation is solid: identity persistence, face-performance attachment, and split-screen support are in place. The primary blocker is the lack of rig-compatible authored hero assets matching the Ziemek/Gniewko concept art. REQUEST_CHANGES: visual quality gate remains open pending asset creation and live capture evidence.
